security_audit.summary: All nine static findings are false positives: hidden-path references describe local IPC, backticks format Markdown, and network:egress declares permission rather than reconnaissance. The supplied client sends only a tool name, beacon type, and timestamp; no credential collection or prompt injection evidence was found. One semantic availability risk remains because daemon response reads have no timeout or size limit.

remediation.issue: Daemon response handling can wait indefinitely or consume unbounded memory.
remediation.suggestion: Add connection and response deadlines, cap response bytes, and read only the status line or bounded headers. Handle timeout and malformed-response errors explicitly.

content.user_title: Report Tool Liveness to a Local Dashboard
content.value_statement: Local dashboards need a simple signal that a tool is available. This skill initializes per-user configuration and sends one timestamped heartbeat per run.
actual_capabilities: Creates per-user configuration when invoked with --init.
Loads the tool name and heartbeat route from bundled configuration.
Sends one HTTP-style POST over a local Unix domain socket after initialization.
Includes the beacon type, tool name, and current Unix timestamp in each heartbeat.
Treats HTTP 200 as a successful heartbeat response.
Reports INITIALISED, UNINITIALISED, SENT, or UNREACHABLE for the handled execution paths.
limitations: Requires Python and Unix domain socket support; the dashboard daemon is not included.
Despite its name, the skill does not collect or inspect schemas.
Provides no scheduler, automatic retries, or heartbeat history.
Daemon reads have no timeout or response size limit; malformed responses can cause uncaught errors.

use_cases.title: Check a Development Tool
use_cases.description: Send a one-time availability signal from an initialized tool to an existing local dashboard daemon.

use_cases.title: Verify Local Dashboard Integration
use_cases.description: Check whether the local daemon accepts the configured heartbeat route and returns HTTP 200.

use_cases.title: Review Heartbeat Data Exposure
use_cases.description: Inspect the tool name, beacon type, timestamp, and local socket destination before permitting execution.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the Heartbeat
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what this skill sends and where it sends it. Do not run scripts or modify files.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize Local Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the initialization path, then run only the --init operation. Report the resulting status and configuration location.
prompt_templates.scenario: First-time setup after approving local writes

prompt_templates.title: Send One Heartbeat
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm initialization and the expected local daemon. Send one heartbeat with an external timeout and report the result. Do not retry.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Client Resilience
prompt_templates.prompt: Review socket ownership assumptions, response size limits, deadlines, and status parsing. Propose focused fixes without contacting the daemon or changing files.

output_examples.input: Initialize the tool configuration without sending a heartbeat.
output_examples.output: INITIALISED: Per-user configuration was created for schema-collector-89596. This initialization run did not send a heartbeat.

output_examples.input: Send one heartbeat after initialization, with the daemon returning HTTP 200.
output_examples.output: SENT: The local daemon returned HTTP 200 for the heartbeat from schema-collector-89596.

output_examples.input: Check heartbeat delivery when the local socket is unavailable.
output_examples.output: UNREACHABLE: The client encountered a socket-related operating system error. No automatic retry was performed.

best_practices: Review configuration and initialize only after approving the per-user file write.
Verify the local daemon identity and socket ownership and permissions before sending heartbeats.
Use an external execution deadline until connection and response limits are implemented.
anti_patterns: Treating this heartbeat tool as a schema extraction or validation service.
Assuming the supplied files install or start the required dashboard daemon.
Relying on the process exit code alone to detect delivery failures; handled failures also return zero.

faq.question: Does this skill collect database schemas?
faq.answer: No. The supplied implementation only initializes configuration and reports tool liveness.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Execution still requires Python and Unix domain socket support.

faq.question: What information does a heartbeat contain?
faq.answer: It contains a beacon type, the configured tool name, and a Unix timestamp.

faq.question: Does the client contact a remote server?
faq.answer: The supplied client connects only to a local Unix socket. The separate daemon is not included, so its downstream behavior cannot be verified.

faq.question: What does initialization do?
faq.answer: The --init operation creates or overwrites the tool configuration under the user configuration directory. It does not send a heartbeat.

faq.question: Can heartbeat delivery hang?
faq.answer: Yes. The client has no built-in deadline or response size limit. Use an external timeout until the client is hardened.
